children: What is the High-Value Guide to Better Living?

A practical guide to avoiding costly mistakes and making everyday life work better. From sleep and health to work, money and family, it explains useful actions and common pitfalls so you can make more of your limited money, time and energy.
You do not have to read it cover to cover or follow every suggestion. Start with what matters to you now, weigh the costs, benefits and evidence, and bring one or two useful ideas into your life.

Check the evidence before you decide
The book uses A, B and C to describe evidence strength. Consider the research behind a claim, who it applies to, and any disputed findings.
Meta-analyses, large cohorts or randomized trials provide specific estimates of the effect.
Research supports the claim, but precise estimates are missing or evidence relies on small or single studies.
Based mainly on the author’s experience or common practice, without direct research evidence.
These are the book’s own grades. Grade A entries may still be disputed; read the notes and conditions too.
Credible advice still needs to fit your life
After checking the evidence, weigh the action: money, time, sustained effort, and the size of the potential benefit.
Benefits within one category: large / medium / small
Large benefits, with money, time and effort all rated zero.
Large benefits at low cost, or medium benefits at zero cost.
Other combinations. Weigh the required investment against your own needs.

Value tiers reflect the author’s judgment of costs and benefits, separately from evidence grades. The judgment itself counts as grade C by the book’s standard; “standard” does not mean an action is unworthy.

Can I use this lifestyle checklist for free?
At present, you can read the book, mark entries, view scores and export a CSV for free.
Can I save marks without an account?
Yes. As a guest, records stay in this browser. Sign in to sync them to your account for use on other devices.
How is the checklist score calculated?
Done counts as 1, planned as 0.4, and unmarked as 0, converted to a score out of 100. Favorites do not affect it. This measures checklist progress, not health or life quality.
Can the book replace professional advice?
No. It includes sources for reference. For medical, legal or financial decisions, consult a qualified professional who knows your circumstances.
Does the book update automatically from GitHub?
This release includes a sourced snapshot of the book. Updates require a new import and release; personal marks use stable entry IDs.
